learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Muscle Artifact.
Apply Muscle Artifact to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Temporalis, frontalis, jaw and neck activity commonly produces irregular fast activity, especially at temporal and frontal electrodes.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Muscle power can dominate beta and gamma bands. Relaxation instructions and observation often outperform post-hoc filtering.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: QEEG high-frequency findings are uninterpretable without rigorous EMG review.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Calling jaw tension “excess cortical beta” is a serious category error.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Muscle Artifact?
options: Temporalis, frontalis, jaw and neck activity commonly produces irregular fast activity, especially at temporal and frontal electrodes.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Muscle Artifact?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Muscle Artifact?

quizBank.explanation: Calling jaw tension “excess cortical beta” is a serious category error.

reviewPrompts.answer: Muscle power can dominate beta and gamma bands. Relaxation instructions and observation often outperform post-hoc filtering.
QEEG high-frequency findings are uninterpretable without rigorous EMG review.
Calling jaw tension “excess cortical beta” is a serious category error.
High-frequency scalp EEG must earn its cerebral interpretation.
